topics.title: Pre-colonial peoples and kingdoms
topics.notes:
Sources of Nigerian history: oral tradition, archaeology (Nok, Igbo-Ukwu, Daima, Ife), architecture, and written records by Arab and European writers and by local authors such as Samuel Johnson (History of the Yorubas). Walter Rodney wrote How Europe Underdeveloped Africa. Cultural lag is the delay between introducing a new trait and society fully accepting it.

Yoruba: the Alaafin ruled Oyo; the Oyomesi council (headed by the Bashorun, like a prime minister) checked him; the Are-Ona-Kakanfo commanded the army; the Ogboni was a Yoruba society. Igbo: an acephalous (no single ruler) society, with the Ofo as the staff of justice and authority, kept by the Okpara (eldest male), and the Ozo title system. Hausa: the head of a city-state is the Sarki; the Hausa Bakwai are Daura, Kano, Zaria, Gobir, Katsina, Rano and Biram. The Fulani are either settled (Town) or pastoral (nomadic). Hausa is the lingua franca of the savanna belt, and the jihad of Usman dan Fodio began in 1804.

Benin: the first dynasty was the Ogiso, and the second dynasty began with Eweka I. The Oba succeeds by primogeniture. Britain took Benin in 1897. The Portuguese were the first Europeans on the coast, and Islam was the first major foreign religion, reaching Nigeria through the Arabs and the trans-Saharan trade before the 15th century.

KEY FORMULA: Alaafin = king; Bashorun = prime minister; Are-Ona-Kakanfo = army chief; Ofo = Igbo authority

topics.title: Colonial rule and nationalism
topics.notes:
Lagos was annexed in 1861. The Berlin Conference was held in 1884/85. Lord Lugard amalgamated the North and South in 1914 and ruled through indirect rule. Colonial education served the colonial administration. The Macpherson Constitution came in 1951.

Nationalists and parties: Herbert Macaulay (father of Nigerian nationalism) founded the NNDP in 1923; the Nigerian Youth Movement began in 1936; Obafemi Awolowo founded the Action Group in 1951; R. A. B. Dikko founded Jam'iyyar Mutanen Arewa; Anthony Enahoro moved the motion for self-government in 1953.

KEY FORMULA: Amalgamation 1914;  NNDP 1923;  NYM 1936;  Macpherson 1951

topics.title: Government and politics
topics.notes:
Nigeria became independent in 1960 and a republic in 1963. The First Republic used a parliamentary system. The Mid-West Region was created in 1963. The first coup was in January 1966 and General Aguiyi-Ironsi became the first military head of state. The civil war lasted from 1967 to 1970. FEDECO was the Federal Electoral Commission. Nigeria has 109 senatorial districts. The University of Benin is in Egor Local Government Area.

KEY FORMULA: Independence 1960;  Republic 1963;  coup Jan 1966;  civil war 1967–1970

topics.title: Culture and society
topics.notes:
Culture is learned, shared and passed on, and its universality means every human society has culture. Values are broad ideals about what is good, right and acceptable. Onwuejeogwu is known for the culture area concept. The relationship between state and individual is a social contract.

KEY FORMULA: Universality = culture exists in every society

topics.title: Citizenship and social justice
topics.notes:
Citizenship by blood or parentage is jus sanguinis; by birthplace it is jus soli. A child born aboard a registered ship takes the nationality tied to the ship's country of registration. Civil rights are protected by the basic laws in the constitution.

KEY FORMULA: Jus sanguinis = blood;  jus soli = soil

topics.title: Education and religion
topics.notes:
The National Curriculum Conference was held in 1969 and led to the National Policy on Education in 1977. The 6-3-3-4 system began in 1981 under President Shagari. WAI was launched in 1984. School is the formal channel of education. Horton and Blyden were early advocates of higher education in West Africa.

Traditional religion believes in a Supreme Being (Olodumare among the Yoruba) and lesser deities. The Igbe movement started among the Urhobo and Isoko. Religion is often confused with sects, cults and denominations.

KEY FORMULA: 6-3-3-4 began 1981;  WAI 1984;  Olodumare = Yoruba Supreme Being
